headline: A 2014 law lets members of the Hoonah Indian Association collect glaucous-winged gull eggs in Glacier Bay National Park under an annual plan.
what_it_does: The law lets the Secretary of the Interior allow Hoonah Indian Association members to collect glaucous-winged gull eggs up to two times a year at up to five locations in Glacier Bay National Park in Alaska. It says this collection is a use the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act specifically permits. The collection schedule and locations must be based on an annual plan prepared by the Secretary and the Association.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Hoonah Indian Association
who_it_affects.how: They may collect gull eggs in Glacier Bay National Park up to two times a year at up to five approved locations, following an annual plan.

who_it_affects.group: The Secretary of the Interior and the National Park Service
who_it_affects.how: They may allow the collection and must prepare the annual plan with the Association that sets its schedule and locations.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on July 25, 2014.
